messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty: SEV2 - geo-routing anomalies detected for requests originating in eu-west1. Alert threshold: error_rate > 5% for 2m. Paging oncall.
pagerduty: paged oncall-sre (maya)
maya: ack - investigating, setting status to investigating :mag:
kevin: saw increased 5xxs in the metric dashboard, spikes started ~3723456700. Mostly from a subset of customers routed to apac nodes.
sophia: confirming, synthetic checks show eu->apac path latency jump + timeouts. example curl:
```
curl -v -H 'Host: api.customer.example' 'https://eu.api.redwood.ai/health' -I
* Connected to eu.api.redwood.ai (35.XXX.XX.XX) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```
raj: interestingly DNS lookups for eu host sometimes resolve to apac pool IPs. suspect routing policy evaluation is choosing wrong region.
emily: any recent deploys to geo-routing service? network-eng?
network-eng: we rolled a small canary of a 'latency-based routing v2' evaluator 30m ago. it changes scoring to prefer probe-weighted latency over region affinity when sample_count > 3. canary was at 10%.
maya: timeline matches. hypothesis: canary mis-evaluated low-sample probes and caused cross-region steering.
oncall-sre: running quick checks - listing route decisions for a few requests:
```
# sample log lines
2026-03-15T12:45:12Z evaluator=v2 sample_count=2 score_apac=12.3 score_eu=11.9 selected=apac
2026-03-15T12:45:13Z evaluator=v2 sample_count=1 score_apac=9.1 score_eu=8.7 selected=apac
```
kevin: sample_count=1/2 is below threshold in v1 but v2 seems to not enforce. that explains why eu clients got routed to apac.
maya: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable v2 evaluator canary rollout 2) enable strict-region-affinity flag 3) push a quick fix that reinserts sample_count check. what looks fastest?
support-lead: need messaging to customers. impact: a subset of EU traffic sees 300-800ms latency increase and some 502s. estimate affected requests ~2-6% of EU traffic. start status page note if we have mitigation.
raj: can we flip canary off remotely? network-eng: yes - canary is controlled by rollout service. I can scale it to 0% in 60s.
network-eng: doing 0% now...
IncidentBot: rollout-service: canary scaled from 10% -> 0% by network-eng at 12:48:20Z
maya: monitoring error graphs... looks like 5xx rate starting to decline
emily: DNS cache TTLs might still point clients to apac for a few minutes. what's current DNS TTL for geo records?
network-eng: eu geo A records TTL is 30s for dynamic entries, but our edge caches sometimes keep older mappings for up to 90s.
kevin: started a cache flush for the edge DNS cluster - command:
```
/ops/dns/flush --region=eu --target=edge-cache-*
```
oncall-sre: flushing now, progress: 8/12 nodes flushed
maya: can we confirm traffic is rebalanced? look at region distribution in LB logs.
oncall-sre: pulling LB logs, sample:
```
2026-03-15T12:49:05Z request_id=abc region_selected=eu backend=eu-12 latency=45ms
2026-03-15T12:49:06Z request_id=def region_selected=eu backend=eu-07 latency=39ms
2026-03-15T12:49:07Z request_id=ghi region_selected=apac backend=apac-03 latency=580ms
```
maya: still seeing some apac selects but trending down. error rate reduced from 6.8% -> 1.6% over last 5m.
support-lead: start draft status message: 'We are investigating elevated errors and latency affecting some EU customers. Mitigation in progress. No data loss.' I'll post an update after we confirm stable.
raj: check downstream caches in customer CDNs too. some clients may have pinned apac ip in their resolver cache for longer.
emily: contacting top 3 affected enterprise customers via SRE-Sales bridge, prepping RCAs.
maya: what's root cause candidate? network-eng: a logic bug in the v2 evaluator where the sample_count guard was accidentally inverted during refactor. when sample_count < threshold it was treated as high-confidence leading to misrouting.
oncall-sre: near-term actions:
- rollback canary (done)
- flush edge dns (in progress)
- enable strict-region-affinity override (will enable if residuals >1% after 2m)
- support outbound notifications (support-lead)
maya: enabling strict-region-affinity flag now as belt-and-braces. doing feature-toggle set region_affinity_override=true for eu at 12:51:10Z
IncidentBot: feature-toggle: region_affinity_override set to true by maya at 12:51:10Z
kevin: after enabling override, residual apac selects dropped below 0.2% and error rate stable at 0.3%.
support-lead: posting status update: 'Mitigation applied: rolled back routing canary and enforced region affinity. Errors and latency returning to normal. Monitoring.' :white_check_mark:
pagerduty: resolved oncall-sre page at 12:53:40Z
maya: ok handing off to network-eng for root cause fix and postmortem. assigning owner = network-eng (raj) to ship patch that reinserts sample_count guard and add unit tests.
raj: will own. patch ETA 24h, will also add a canary safety check that prevents rollout >0% unless simulated probe coverage > 5.
emily: support team will follow up with affected customers and offer incident summary.
kevin: add follow-ups for runbook updates: include checklist for canary rollbacks and quick DNS flush steps.
sophia: oncall handoff note for next shift: system stable, watch geo error rate and LB region distribution for 2h. handoff to kevin in ~45m.
oncall-sre: leaving a couple of useful queries for follow-up:
```
# error rate by geo
select time, error_rate from metrics where service='geo-router' group by geo
# route decision log filter
grep 'evaluator=v2' /var/log/geo-router/decision.log | tail -n 200
```
maya: documented incident timeline and mitigation steps in the incident tracker. tagging postmortem owner = raj.
support-lead: customers notified, status page updated at 12:55Z. no further immediate customer escalations.
network-eng: I'll prepare patch and tests this evening. thanks everyone. closing slack thread when handoff confirmed.
kevin: thanks - great coordination. :thumbsup:
maya: handing off now - stable. handing off to kevin for ongoing watch.
kevin: ack, taking watch. will escalate if we see new anomalies.
